prior_art.decode: R1185 opened: NLS_MSS_7913_127, Jean de Saint-Maurice, Dijon, to Granvelle, 5 July 1548. Status DECRYPTED, with two key documents attached ('Granvelle-Saint Mauris Cipher (1548) [key]' and 'Cipher between Charles V and Jean de Saint-Mauris (1547) [key]') and a note crediting Tomokiyo's reconstruction (reported 21 Jan 2019). The lead's 'Cryptoole status open' is misleading: that merged row also carries our own source.
prior_art.tomokiyo: This letter is Tomokiyo's source. spanish2.htm, 'Granvelle-Saint Mauris Cipher (1547-1548)' (local targets/adrian1521/spanish2.htm): the cipher was reconstructed from this letter (BNE MSS/7913/127), with a marginal decipherment he calls hard to read; he works through its cipher paragraphs. Key table published. His blog of Jan 2019 also announces it.
prior_art.lasry: Not Lasry's letter. GL.htm has no Saint Mauris entry. Tomokiyo credits Lasry with breaking another letter in this family (Simancas EST,LEG,1381,143, 24 Aug 1551) and with telling him of the 2022 result; nothing shows Lasry worked on this one.
prior_art.edition: No print of the plaintext found. Potter, 'La fin du règne de François Ier ... d'après les dépêches de Jean de Saint-Mauris (1547)' (Cour de France.fr) describes the cipher, per Tomokiyo; the Cassan 1878 edition is of 1547 despatches. Neither was read for this 1548 letter; Papiers d'État not searched by date.
prior_art.literature: Pierrot, Desenclos, Gaudry and Zimmermann, 'Deciphering Charles Quint', HistoCrypt 2023 (text read): cites MSS/7913/127 by name as an 'isolated encrypted letter' and says Tomokiyo's 2022 reconstruction 'relied on a single letter' from BNE 7913, convergent with theirs. Pich-Ponce 2023 PP1 is the same cipher, used in 100+ letters to 1554.
